verdict: The cluster builds all three brief items. Item 1, asking for different terms, is built: the player asks once, while the offer stands, for a shorter term, voice-over added or the UK and Australia added. The office answers two days later at a labeled chance computed from interestOf. The terms are kept as versions on Agreement.deal and read by the term's end (proagent.ts:1250, endedWords), by the commission (coveredUnder in propay.ts:356), by the offers the agent handles (projobs.ts:1749, 1769) and by the agent's submissions (submitsFor in reachOf, projobs.ts:674). The commission cap is untouched. Item 2, the voice department, is built: Halberd's voice-over department and the invented Celia Brannock, the 'voice' field and the 'demo' material. Her office asks for a demo, weighs it as a reel's band, offers a voice-over agreement, takes commission on voice work and submits for all four voice kinds. Item 3, the festival introduction, is built as a route and an exported introduceAtFestival, tested directly. Every new piece of state has a reader except two audit-only fields (DealVersion.how and .ask). Save schema stays 94 in both pins, and an agreement shaped as BASE wrote it loads, takes an ask and ends at its term. tsc on the app config and eslint are clean. All 25 existing affected files I ran pass except b20-guide-wiring, whose wiring list is a shared record. Two blocking defects remain. (1) Downstream contradiction: contracts.ts:239 still writes "Voice-over work is outside an agent's agreement, so no commission is owed on it" into every voice part's contract, while the pay now takes 10% under an agreement that covers voice-over. (2) Weak test: no test proves the answer actually depends on how keen the office is. Making the draw ignore the stored chance survives every test, because the journeys only use draws under 0.1 or at least 0.9. Several comments the change made false are left in the present tense. The festival route is promised in player text but nothing outside tests calls it until the festivals cluster lands.

findings.claim: Every voice part's contract still says voice-over work is outside an agent's agreement and owes no commission. Under an agreement that covers voice-over (Celia Brannock's, or Thomas Ashgrove's with voice-over added), the pay now takes 10% on the same engagement, and the Work tab shows both.
findings.evidence: src/engine/systems/contracts.ts:239: `if (voiceOnlyFormat(fmt.workflow)) out.push({ kind: 'rule', id: 'voice-over', words: 'Voice-over work is outside an agent’s agreement, so no commission is owed on it.' });` is unconditional. WorkPane.tsx:422 renders e.contract.clauses. Probe P1, a lantern-row booking under a voice-scope agreement: the clause was present, and commissionOn returned amount 90000, how 'term', '10% of $9,000.00 gross…'. tests/career-workflows.test.ts:628 still asserts the clause on every voice contract; its comment was changed to 'outside a legit agent's agreement', but the code was not.
findings.suggested_fix: Build the clause from the engagement's agreement. In contractFor, look up owedAgreement or the agreement in force and call coveredUnder. Say the no-commission sentence only when the agreement leaves voice-over out, or when nobody represents the actor. Otherwise say commission is owed under the agreement with the agency. Add a test with a voice-covered agreement that asserts the clause and commissionOn agree.

findings.claim: No test proves the office's answer depends on how keen it is. The brief asks for a labeled chance reading interestOf. The answer could ignore the stored chance, or use any fixed figure between 0.1 and 0.9, and all 18 tests would still pass.
findings.evidence: Mutation A: representation.ts:315 changed `< ask.chance` to `< TERMS.base[ask.what]`. b27-representation passed 15/15 and b27-representation-screen 3/3. The journeys pick lives with `u < TERMS.least` (test line 102: `lifeWhere('rep-yes', (u) => u < TERMS.least)`) or `u >= TERMS.most` (line 156), so any chance gives the same outcome. The 'chance tracks keenness' test (lines 170-181) only checks termsChance and askChance, never the answer. The decider pro.agent_terms calls termsChance and termsDraw directly, not answerAsk.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a falsifiability twin. Pick a life whose draw falls between two chances: for example, a draw between the chance at the current factors and the chance after one more missed meeting, which lowers reliability. Make the same ask in both. Assert one life is agreed and the other kept, and that ask.chance is the figure the panel showed.

findings.claim: When no festival name is passed, introduceAtFestival names the Sundance Film Festival rather than the entry's own institution. It also says the film 'screened' for an entry that is only selected. Once the festivals cluster adds Cannes, Venice, the Berlinale and IDFA entries, a call without a name would put Sundance on a film it never showed.
findings.evidence: representation.ts:355: `const name = festival ?? `the ${entry.year} Sundance Film Festival`;`. Line 352 accepts `entry.state === 'selected'`. The notice and history at lines 363, 371-378 say 'where ${film.project} screened'. FestivalEntry has `institution` (awards.ts:87).
findings.suggested_fix: Derive the name from entry.institution through the awards content's institution names, or require the name argument. Word the selected-but-unscreened case as 'selected' rather than 'screened', or accept only 'screened'.

findings.claim: The guide's career.agreement entry still says the agreement ends 'when its year is up', which is false for a six-month agreement. The new career.agreement-terms example states a 7-in-10 chance as a certain result.
findings.evidence: guide/career.ts:516: 'It can end by agreement at any time, or under Equity’s or SAG-AFTRA’s rules, or when its year is up.' The same entry's first paragraph was edited to mention the six months.
